items.title: How to Get Love Less Wrong: George Saunders on Breaking the Patterns that Break Our Hearts
items.description: "We want to believe that love is singular and exclusive, and it unnerves us to think that it might actually be renewable..."

items.title: How to Help Someone Change: The Samurai Guide to Giving Feedback
items.description: Few things in life are more exasperating than seeing the potential in someone you love and seeing them continually fall short of it, stumbling again and again over the same self-erected roadblocks of character and conduct, comporting themselves in a manner painfully inferior to what you know them to be capable of. items.title: How to Be a Lichen: Adaptive Strategies for the Vulnerabilities of Being Human from Nature’s Tiny Titans of Tenacity
items.description: When I was a child, little delighted me more than the magical green garlands draping from the pine trees, which I made into wreaths and mustaches to roam the mountains of Bulgaria as a miniature Orlando. I had no idea that Usnea longissima is just one of more than 20,000 known species of lichen — almost twice as many as birds. items.title: How to Love: Legendary Zen Buddhist Teacher Thich Nhat Hanh on Mastering the Art of “Interbeing”
items.description: "To love without knowing how to love wounds the person we love."

items.title: How to Grow Old: Bertrand Russell on What Makes a Fulfilling Life
items.description: "Make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal, until bit by bit the walls of the ego recede, and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life."

items.title: Borges on How to Conquer Time
items.description: "Time is the substance I am made of. Time is a river which sweeps me along, but I am the river; it is a tiger which destroys me, but I am the tiger; it is a fire which consumes me, but I am the fire."

items.title: The Wild Iris: Nobel Laureate Louise Glück on the Door at the End of Your Suffering
items.description: "Whatever returns from oblivion returns to find a voice."

items.title: How to Bear Your Sorrows: Nick Cave on Integrating the Darkness of Loss with the Bright Ongoingness of Life
items.description: Few things in our culture are more wounding than the concept of healing — as if the pains and losses that we suffer are an illness, a malfunction of the psyche to be cut out like a tumor, rather than a natural function of being alive, of feeling life deeply and living it fully. items.title: How to Spot and How to Stop a Liar: Hannah Arendt on Deception, Self-Deception, and the Psychology of Defactualization
items.description: "No matter how large the tissue of falsehood that an experienced liar has to offer, it will never be large enough ... to cover the immensity of factuality."

items.title: Marcus Aurelius on the Good Luck of Your Bad Luck: The Stoic Strategy for Weathering Life’s Waves and Turning Suffering into Strength
items.description: "What happened could have happened to anyone, but not everyone could have carried on."

items.title: The Four Buddhist Mantras for Turning Fear into Love
items.description: "When you love someone, the best thing you can offer that person is your presence."

items.title: De Profundis: Patti Smith Reads Oscar Wilde’s Stirring Letter on Suffering and Transcendence, Penned in Prison
items.description: "I have got to make everything that has happened to me good for me... There is not a single degradation of the body which I must not try and make into a spiritualising of the soul."

items.title: Fernando Pessoa on Unselfing into Who You Really Are

E. Cummings wrote in his timeless summons for the courage to be yourself. items.title: Diseases of the Will: Neuroscience Founding Father Santiago Ramón y Cajal on the Six Psychological Flaws That Keep the Gifted from Living Up to Their Gift
items.description: "Our neurons must be used ... not only to know but also to transform knowledge; not only to experience but also to construct."
